notes: West 2007 ch. 4 names the case forms of Father Sky beyond the vocative: 'Homeric πατρὸς Διός, Διὶ πατρί; Italic … Iuve patre'; Schmitt 1967 §288 lists the eight Iguvine instances (IIa 5, 10; IIb 7, 17, 22, 24, 26; III 22). Revised after round 4: the line is cut to the shared dative NP, as a bare np utterance in the dative ('to Father Sky', the god an offering or prayer is addressed to). The earlier imperative 'make a vow' had the o-grade causative *h₁wogʷʰéye- of Lat. voveō, which stood only in a support ref (Cato Agr. 83.1, now dropped) and in neither parallel passage: Gk εὔχομαι is an e-grade thematic middle with no usable lexeme, and Umbr. vufru is an adjective of the calf ('votive'), not a verb (r4). Greek: Διὶ πατρί after εὐξάμενος/-οι (Il. 17.498, Od. 13.51) and after σπεῖσον (Il. 24.287–288), all checked in AGDT. Umbrian (Buck 1904 OCR, checked; Tab. Ig. II is not in the UD treebank): IIb 21–23 vitlu vufru … sestu Iuvepatre (Buck: 'vitulum votivum … sistito Iovi patri') and IIb 26 … fetu Iuvepatre ('facito Iovi patri'); IIb 7 Afmune Iuve patre fetu writes the two words apart. Support: IIb 17–18 Iuvepatre with the prayer verb prepesnimu. Latin Cato Agr. 134.1 (LASLA, checked: Iano Ioui Iunoni praefato) has the dative of the god but not 'father', so it counts for *dyḗws only. Morphology: dative singular in both nouns, as in Διὶ πατρί and Iuve patre; Gk Διϝί has the zero grade *diw-éy of the engine, Umbr. Iuve the analogical full grade also seen in Lat. Iovī. Father is in apposition to the god's name (Ζεύς, πατήρ as two words; Iuve patre written apart in IIb 7). Builder gaps: Umbr. Iuve is in no table (Buck §183 gives Iuve as the dat. sg. beside O. Diúvei, L. Iovī), and Iuvepatre reaches *dyḗws and *ph₂tḗr only through the compound (evidence from a compound member). Same lexemes as sky-father-001/-003 (*dyéw ph₂ter): one evaluation group, though here the dative stands in both branches and the second branch is Italic.
